svg.text: Repaso — the whole system on one page
A parent photographs a notebook page; the child practices in the same chat, and a person is interrupted only on evidence.
3 Strands graphs · 13 agents · a deterministic harness underneath all of it · 100 % of model calls on Amazon Bedrock.
a photo of the notebook page
The parent is the only account holder. The student has
no account and no name — an alias only. The teacher
installs nothing and reads only what the parent sends.
↑ everything the family receives comes back up this line, from delivery at the foot of the runtime
the AWS transport spine — one webhook in, one long turn out
secret token checked at the edge
Telegram retries a webhook that does not answer within seconds, and a
tutoring turn takes longer than that. Lambda acknowledges and hands off;
the worker then takes as long as the work honestly takes.
one alarm per family — the agent
reschedules its own for exam mode
The deterministic harness — the plane every graph above stands on
no model decides pedagogy here: same input, same output, every run, offline. This is the half a school can audit — and the half that fires the alarms.
session · plan — when an item comes back
response · apply — the level, and its cold start
ingest · parse — blur floor, ask for a re-photo
every stage — exactly once, even after a crash
every model call — a declared hard ceiling
every graph — injected, never a wall-clock read
close · engagement — rest days, holidays and
outage days masked before any alert can fire
Local mode runs this whole plane with
no LLM at all — a strict playback double
raises on any unplanned model call.
every node traced in AgentCore Observability · L1 session memory held per family · the runtime executes our graphs, it does not decide anything
Our code — 3 Strands graphs from 4 builders (session and response are the two halves of the tutor loop) · 13 agents
nodes in execution order; each chip names the node, the model behind it, and the agent or harness module that runs it. Green = no model involved.
one node, two agents — an item ships only if both accept
One capsule per student per day: the SM-2 review queue plus one slot the planner reserves for unseen material, so a strong
student still meets new work. Composed for a nine-year-old, checked by the legibility harness, and never sent on a rest day.
A grade below 0.85 confidence quarantines: a grade that is
not sure does not exist, and no one is told anything about it.
escalate is a conditional edge — STRUGGLING ∧ ≥ 9 attempts
∧ a 7-day cooldown per student, or the graph ends here.
A cohort note needs k ≥ 3 distinct families in the same section
× competency, and fires at most once per ISO week.
Items retire on point-biserial discrimination, not on a hunch.
cohort reuses the response graph's escalation composer — which
is why the fleet is 13 agents across 15 nodes, not 14.
Conditional edges are real: a graph that has nothing to say ends without saying it, and the run costs nothing further.
every message is claimed exactly once — a retried event never sends the same thing twice · quiet hours and the family calendar are honoured before anything leaves
100 % of model calls · no other provider · every role declares its own fallback chain
items, capsules, open-answer grading, escalation and cohort notes
competency mapper, adaptation policy — schema-bound, cheap, fast
the Armor screen and the answerability probe — the two smallest jobs
what is remembered where, and which tier is the system of record
the running conversation, held per family
short-lived; never the system of record
what the mapper matches new material against
L3 · DynamoDB single table + grade log
the system of record; grades are append-only
all of it CDK, all of it namespaced repaso-*
S3 + KMS — notebook photos and voice notes, encrypted at rest
DynamoDB PITR + RETAIN — a stack delete does not delete a history
EventBridge Scheduler — one alarm per family, moved by the agent
SQS dead-letter queues — 3 receives, then a human looks
AgentCore Observability — every node, claim and refusal traced
AWS Budgets — one alarm per declared spend limit
API Gateway secret token — the webhook is not a public endpoint
Local mode reproduces every one of these behind a file-backed
double: 706 tests, zero credentials, zero network, ~5 seconds.
Measured, not asserted — every number traces to a dated report in docs/reports/
9 attack families, ES + EN, including OCR-corrupted variants.
0 % false blocks on 200 clean grade-4 texts — including the
near-miss strings written to trip the screener.
Zero credentials. Zero network. Graphs, harness, Armor and
calendar all run on a laptop against a strict playback double
that raises on any unplanned model call.
pytest -q · local mode, not one Bedrock call
30 students × 14 days through the real pipeline.
transcript for the same seed, on any machine.
Per 100 student-weeks, calendar mask and delivery-health gate
on: 0 across 2,400 student-weeks, gate A 20/20 seeds. The
pre-fix control arm still fires 1,689 — 70.4 per 100.
Masking must not buy quiet by going blind: every genuine
dropout alerted within 3 practicable days — including the one
whose silence starts on the first outage day (20/20).
p50 and p95 over 40 virgin seeds — the interruption budget a
family actually lives with. 7 of 8 pre-registered gates pass;
G2, zero false-positive students, stays red on the board.
the recall that killed a fix
A corroboration floor promised to cut the residual false
positives. Its own pre-declared protocol measured recall fall
0.994 → 0.917. Falsified in four hours, reverted the same hour.

Open, and on the board: 11 residual struggle false positives across the 40 virgin seeds keep gate G2 below its 95 % bar. The root cause is the EMA's cold start — three consecutive misses multiply the estimate by 0.7³ from any prior history.

Threshold-level guards are exhausted: two swept, one slab-confirmed, one falsified. The remaining fix is the estimator itself — a BKT-style slip/guess separation — and it is on the roadmap rather than in this drawing.
